samples.summary: CollabDocumentProvider now calls fetchMe unconditionally, and it is mounted on the anonymous share-link route — a 401 there triggers logout() + hard redirect to /login
samples.evidence: `CollabDocumentProvider` gained `useQuery({queryKey:['me'], queryFn: fetchMe, retry:false})` (packages/frontend/src/components/collab-document-provider.tsx:152-156). It is rendered on the PUBLIC share route at packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:979, 998, 1007, 1022, 1035 (and, for shared PDFs, via `PdfCollabProvider` at packages/frontend/src/app/files/pdf-collab.tsx:199). `fetchMe` goes through `fetchWithAuth`, which on a 401 whose refresh fails calls `logout({redirect:false,...})` and then `redirectTo("/login")` — `window.location.href = '/login'` (packages/frontend/src/api/auth.ts:213-227). That route deliberately uses `fetchMeOptional` with key `['me','optional']` (shared-document.tsx:900-904) precisely to avoid this. An anonymous share-link visitor is now bounced to the login page. Fix belongs on the new code: use `fetchMeOptional` / the existing `['me','optional']` query, or skip the query outside PrivateRoute.

samples.summary: Share links are only excluded from the durable path for ANONYMOUS visitors; a signed-in user opening a share link gets a nested client with the owner token instead of the share token
samples.evidence: The design doc claims the exclusion is structural — docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:81-90 and :233 say `shared-document.tsx` mounts its own provider and is therefore excluded — but `shared-document.tsx:979` renders `CollabDocumentProvider`, and the implementation's only share-link guard is `!me` (collab-document-provider.tsx:186). A signed-in user visiting a share link for a document they do not own has `me` defined, so with the preference on the durable branch nests `DurableYorkieProvider` with `authTokenInjector={fetchYorkieToken}` (collab-document-provider.tsx:198), overriding the outer provider's `fetchYorkieShareToken(token)` (shared-document.tsx:976) — the attach would carry owner credentials the auth webhook will reject, and the shared document's content would be persisted to disk under that user's scope. Latent today only because `@yorkie-js/react` is pinned to 0.7.22 (packages/frontend/package.json:65) so `supportsClientKey()` is false.

samples.summary: LossWatch calls useDocument() above the DocumentProvider it is meant to watch, so expectLoss can never latch in the real tree
samples.evidence: `DurableYorkieProvider` renders `<LockRefusalWatch><LossWatch store={store}>{children}</LossWatch></LockRefusalWatch>` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:98-100), and `children` here is the `inner` element that CONTAINS the `DocumentProvider` (collab-document-provider.tsx:160-165, 206). `LossWatch` therefore calls `useDocument()` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:120) outside any `DocumentProvider`, so it either throws or yields no doc, and `store.expectLoss(...)` is never called. Per the store's own contract that is exactly the failure it warns about: `remove` is called on every ordinary detach, so without the latch nothing is archived on real losses (packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts `expectLoss` docs). The new test hides this because `useDocument` is mocked to return a doc regardless of provider nesting (packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:34-44).

samples.summary: The only production caller of deriveSyncState never supplies `durable`, so the new `saved-locally` state is unreachable; and when it is wired, the unsaved-work navigation/beforeunload guard will stop registering
samples.evidence: `use-sync-status.ts:214` calls `deriveSyncState({ connected, pending, syncFailed })` with no `durable`, so the new branch (sync-state.ts:85) can never fire in the app. Separately, `sync-status-chip.tsx:106` computes `stranded = state === 'not-saved'` and `mayHaveUnsent = stranded || state === 'saving'` drives both the `beforeunload` handler (line 119-130) and `useNavigationGuard` (line 142) — once `durable` is threaded through, a document in `saved-locally` will silently lose both guards. Whether that is intended is not stated anywhere in the diff.

samples.summary: The store-key parsing rule is duplicated: `documentIdOf` in offline-copy.ts reimplements the exported `documentKeyOf`, the exact drift the store warns about
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/lib/wafflebase-doc-store.ts` exports `documentKeyOf` and its doc comment says it lives there "because two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false"; `durable-session.ts:1` imports it. `offline-copy.ts:47-50` defines a private `documentIdOf` with the same `split('/')` logic instead of importing it — a second copy that can drift if the SDK's key shape changes.

samples.summary: Nothing in the app wires the preference toggle, the erase watcher, or stale collection — the whole offline subsystem has no production entry point yet
samples.evidence: Outside `*.test.*`, there is no reference to `setOfflinePersistenceEnabled`, `useOfflinePersistenceEnabled` (only `use-durable-document.ts:73`), `watchForOfflineDisable`, `eraseOfflineData`, `collectStale`, `listRecoverableWork` or `recoverOfflineCopy`. In particular `watchForOfflineDisable` is never started, so the Settings promise the module's own docstring quotes ("turning this off deletes them") has no caller, and `collectStale` never runs, so stored entries are never collected.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. CollabDocumentProvider unconditionally issues useQuery({queryKey:['me'], queryFn: fetchMe, retry:false}) at collab-document-provider.tsx:152-156 with no `enabled` gate. That component is rendered on the anonymous share route at shared-document.tsx:979, 998, 1007, 1022, 1035, and App.tsx:119 mounts `/shared/:token` outside the PrivateRoute group (App.tsx:128), so unauthenticated visitors reach it. fetchMe (auth.ts:116-123) routes through fetchWithAuth, which on a 401 with a failed refresh calls logout({redirect:false,...}) and redirectTo('/login') → window.location.href (auth.ts:220-228, 53-62); redirectTo has no public-route guard. The route's own deliberate mitigation uses a different cache key (['me','optional'] with fetchMeOptional, shared-document.tsx:900-904; fetchMeOptional returns null on 401 at auth.ts:136-162), so it does not suppress the new ['me'] query. The QueryClient is a default `new QueryClient()` (App.tsx:89), so the query fires on mount. The provider's own doc comment (collab-document-provider.tsx:137-140) claims share links are 'excluded structurally' because shared-document.tsx mounts its own provider — that claim is contradicted by the five CollabDocumentProvider call sites in that very file. This is a behaviour change to an exported symbol breaking a consumer outside the diff: critical and blocking under the blast-radius rubric.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element checks out in the repo. shared-document.tsx:979/998/1007 render CollabDocumentProvider inside a share-scoped YorkieProvider whose authTokenInjector is fetchYorkieShareToken(token) (shared-document.tsx:976). CollabDocumentProvider's only share-relevant guard is `!me` (collab-document-provider.tsx:185); the sole key-based exclusion is `pdf-` (use-durable-document.ts:31-33), so nothing excludes share-link docKeys (doc-/slides-/note-). A signed-in share-link visitor resolves `me` because the provider issues its own ["me"]/fetchMe query (collab-document-provider.tsx:152-156), independent of the route's ["me","optional"]/fetchMeOptional query (shared-document.tsx:900-904). On that branch DurableYorkieProvider mounts a nested KeyedYorkieProvider forwarding authTokenInjector=fetchYorkieToken (collab-document-provider.tsx:198; durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:90-101), overriding the share token, and attaches a WafflebaseDocStore keyed to that user (use-durable-document.ts:157), persisting the shared document under their scope. The design doc asserts the opposite invariant (docs/design/offline-local-persistence.md:81-91), so the exclusion is documented-but-unenforced. The only thing suppressing it today is the build-time pin: supportsClientKey() is false with @yorkie-js/react 0.7.22 (package.json:65) vs MinClientKeyVersion 0.7.23 (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24,61-67) — but that file itself says bumping the dependency is the only action needed to enable the feature, so it is a feature switch, not a guard on this path, and does not support refutation. Blast-radius lane (consumer outside the diff bypassing/violating the changed component's stated exclusion); major impact: wrong auth credentials on attach plus off-scope disk persistence of shared content.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. LossWatch calls useDocument() at durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:122 while being rendered as the PARENT of `children` (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:99); its sole caller passes `inner`, which is the element containing the DocumentProvider (collab-document-provider.tsx:163-168, 206). React context resolves by rendered position, so LossWatch's hook is above the DocumentProvider. This repo documents that useDocument() throws outside a DocumentProvider (site-header.tsx:23-30; sandbox replica of the real dist at design-sandbox/src/scenes/canvas/yorkie-offline.tsx:91-93 and :304). So the subscription either crashes the durable tree or never runs. Grep shows expectLoss has exactly one production caller — durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:127 — and the store contract (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:628-647, 649-662) states `remove` is called on ordinary detach too and only expectLoss distinguishes a loss, so unarchived data loss follows. The new test masks this by mocking @yorkie-js/react so DocumentProvider is a passthrough and useDocument returns a doc regardless of nesting (collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx:24-47, 184-201). In-lane: a cross-file invariant ("mounted inside a DocumentProvider") violated at the only call site.
